items.q: You want to change a volume from milliliters to liters. Which conversion factor do you multiply by?

why.correct: The unit you want goes on top and the unit you have goes on the bottom: 1 L / 1000 mL.
options: This factor is upside down: mL would end up squared instead of canceling.
Milli means one thousandth, not one hundredth; 100 belongs to centi.
Right: liters on top, milliliters on the bottom, so mL cancels and L is left.
A liter is larger than a milliliter, so 1000 L can never equal 1 mL.

items.q: A hiking trail is 2.45 km long. How long is it in meters?

mistakes.why: Value: you divided by 1000. A meter is smaller than a kilometer, so the number of meters must be larger.

why.correct: 2.45 km × (1000 m / 1 km) = 2450 m. Kilo means 1000, so the number gets 1000 times larger as the unit gets 1000 times smaller.

items.q: A metal block has a mass of 12.6 g and a volume of 4.65 cm³. What is its density? Include the unit.

mistakes.why: Value: you divided volume by mass. Density is mass divided by volume, in g/cm³.

why.correct: Density = mass ÷ volume = 12.6 g ÷ 4.65 cm³ = 2.71 g/cm³. The unit comes straight from the division: grams per cubic centimeter.

items.q: Ethanol has a density of 0.789 g/mL. What is the mass of 250.0 mL of ethanol, in grams?

mistakes.why: Value: you divided by the density, which leaves mL²/g. Multiply by g/mL so that mL cancels.

why.correct: 250.0 mL × (0.789 g / 1 mL) = 197 g. The density works as a conversion factor: mL cancels, g is left.

items.q: Normal body temperature is 37.0 °C. What is it in kelvin?

mistakes.why: Value: you subtracted 273.15. To go from °C to K, add 273.15.

why.correct: K = °C + 273.15 = 37.0 + 273.15 = 310.2 K. A kelvin is the same size as a Celsius degree; the scale just starts at absolute zero.

items.q: Which setup converts 3.5 hours into seconds?

why.correct: Chain one factor per step, each with the unit you have on the bottom: h → min → s. 3.5 × 60 × 60 = 12,600 s.
options: Both factors are upside down: the units multiply into h²/s instead of canceling.
The first factor works, but the second puts seconds on the bottom, giving min²/s.
There are 3600 seconds in an hour, not 60, so this answer is 60 times too small.
Right: hours cancel, then minutes cancel, and seconds are left.

items.q: Put the steps for solving a unit conversion with dimensional analysis in order.
options: Write the given quantity with its unit
Choose a factor with the given unit on the bottom
Add factors until only the wanted unit is left
Multiply the numbers and cancel the units
Check that the size of the answer makes sense

why.correct: Start from the given quantity, build the chain of factors, cancel units, then do the arithmetic and check the answer with a quick estimate.

items.q: A student converts 4250 mg to kilograms and reports 4,250,000,000 kg. What went wrong?
options: The student used 100 mg per gram in place of 1000 mg per gram
Milligrams and kilograms measure different things
Both factors were upside down, so the number grew instead of shrinking
The student should have added 1000 instead of multiplying

why.correct: The right answer is 4250 mg × (1 g / 1000 mg) × (1 kg / 1000 g) = 0.00425 kg. A kilogram is a million times larger than a milligram, so the number must shrink.
options: A wrong 100 would give a different error; the reported answer comes from correct factors of 1000 used upside down.
Both measure mass, and any mass unit can be converted to any other with the right factors.
Right: mg → g and g → kg each make the number smaller. Flipping both makes it a million times larger instead of smaller.
Unit conversions multiply or divide by a factor; adding a number changes the quantity itself.

items.q: A medicine dose is 15 mg per kilogram of body mass. How many grams does a 42 kg patient receive?

mistakes.why: Value: you divided body mass by the dose. Multiply: kg cancels against "per kg", leaving mg, then change mg to g.

why.correct: 42 kg × (15 mg / 1 kg) × (1 g / 1000 mg) = 0.63 g. The dose rate is a conversion factor from body mass to medicine mass.

items.q: Why can a temperature in kelvin not be negative?
options: Zero kelvin is absolute zero, the coldest temperature possible
The kelvin scale counts in steps that are smaller than the degrees of the Celsius scale
Scientists agreed to drop the negative half of the Celsius scale
Kelvin is used for gases, which stop existing below zero

why.correct: The kelvin scale starts at absolute zero (−273.15 °C), the coldest possible temperature, so every real temperature in kelvin is positive.
options: Right: the kelvin scale starts at absolute zero, so nothing can be colder than 0 K.
A kelvin and a Celsius degree are the same size; only the starting point differs.
The zero point is set by nature, at the coldest possible temperature, not by an agreement to drop numbers.
The scale applies to any substance; it starts at absolute zero, not at a property of gases.

items.q: Which of these are SI base units? Select all that apply.
options: kilogram (kg)
liter (L)
kelvin (K)
degree Celsius (°C)

why.correct: The kilogram and the kelvin are base units. The liter is built from the meter, and Celsius is a scale shifted from kelvin.
options: Right: the SI base unit of mass is the kilogram, not the gram.
The liter is a common volume unit, but it is defined from the meter (1 L = 1 dm³), so it is not a base unit.
Right: the kelvin is the SI base unit of temperature.
Celsius is a common scale, but the SI base unit of temperature is the kelvin.

items.q: Water has a density of 1.00 g/mL. A 30.0 g plastic bead takes up 25.0 mL. Will the bead float or sink in water, and why?
options: Float: its density, 0.833 g/mL, is less than that of water
Sink: its density, 1.20 g/mL, is greater than that of water
Sink: its mass, 30.0 g, is greater than 1.00 g
Float: its volume, 25.0 mL, is greater than 1.00 mL

why.correct: Density = 30.0 g ÷ 25.0 mL = 1.20 g/mL. An object denser than water sinks.
options: This divides volume by mass. Density is mass ÷ volume.
Right: 30.0 g ÷ 25.0 mL = 1.20 g/mL, which is more than 1.00 g/mL.
Floating depends on mass per volume, not on mass alone; a heavy wooden beam still floats.
A large volume alone does not decide it; you need mass divided by volume.

items.q: A runner covers 5.0 km in 25 min. Which setup gives the speed in meters per second?

why.correct: 5.0 km/25 min × 1000 m/km × 1 min/60 s = 3.3 m/s. A unit on the bottom (min) needs a factor with that unit on top to cancel.
options: Both factors are upside down: the units come out as km²·s/(m·min²).
Right: km cancels to leave m on top, and min cancels to leave s on the bottom.
This starts from minutes per kilometer, the inverse of a speed.
The meters are right, but seconds end up on top, giving m·s/min².
